title: Podman no longer works when the CMD.EXE session is closed
body:
### Issue Description

When I start the Podman machine in a CMD.EXE window, Podman works as expected. But when I close the CMD.EXE window, Podman no longer works. After stopping and starting the machine Podman works again.

It appears podman.exe remains running after `podman machine start`. And remains attached to the CMD.EXE process. When the CMD.EXE process is stopped, podman.exe is killed and Podman no longer works.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Start a CMD.EXE window.

Nothing is running.

```
C>tasklist | findstr "podman.exe gvproxy.exe"
```

Start Podman machine.

```
C>podman machine start
Starting machine "podman-machine-default"

This machine is currently configured in rootless mode. If your containers
require root permissions (e.g. ports < 1024), or if you run into compatibility
issues with non-podman clients, you can switch using the following command:

        podman machine set --rootful

API forwarding listening on: npipe:////./pipe/docker_engine
Docker API clients default to this address. You do not need to set DOCKER_HOST.

Machine "podman-machine-default" started successfully
```

podman.exe and gvproxy.exe are running.

```
C>tasklist | findstr "podman.exe gvproxy.exe"
gvproxy.exe                   9816 Console                    1     41.396 K
podman.exe                   13764 Console                    1     39.128 K
```

Podman works (I have no containers running).

```
C>podman ps
CONTAINER ID  IMAGE       COMMAND     CREATED     STATUS      PORTS       NAMES
```

Trying to stop the CMD.EXE sessions keeps the window open. Close with Ctrl+C or "X" button.

```
C>exit
```

Start a new CMD.EXE window.

gvproxy.exe is still running.

```
C>tasklist | findstr "podman.exe gvproxy.exe"
gvproxy.exe                   9816 Console                    1     42.192 K
```

Podman no longer works.

```
C>podman ps
Cannot connect to Podman. Please verify your connection to the Linux system using `podman system connection list`, or try `podman machine init` and `podman machine start` to manage a new Linux VM
Error: unable to connect to Podman socket: Get "http://d/v6.1.0/libpod/_ping": ssh: rejected: connect failed (open failed)
```

We can still SSH into the machine. But /etc/containers is not accessible.

```
C>podman machine ssh
Connecting to vm podman-machine-default. To close connection, use `~.` or `exit`
Fedora CoreOS 44.20260707.3.1
Tracker: https://github.com/coreos/fedora-coreos-tracker
Discuss: https://discussion.fedoraproject.org/tag/coreos

Last login: Mon Aug 17 13:01:21 2026 from 192.168.127.1
Failed to obtain podman configuration: open /etc/containers/storage.conf: input/output error
```

```
core@localhost:~$ file /etc
/etc: directory
core@localhost:~$ file /etc/containers
/etc/containers: cannot open `/etc/containers' (Input/output error)
core@localhost:~$ findmnt -T /etc
TARGET SOURCE                                                          FSTYPE OPTIONS
/etc   /dev/sda4[/ostree/deploy/fedora-coreos/deploy/f4e7417c3ccaa6e287de2a45626e872b2d39bdcdf01e4c60fb8a2757ff80313c.0/etc]
                                                                       xfs    rw,relatime,seclabel,inode64,logbufs=8,log
core@localhost:~$ findmnt -T /etc/containers
TARGET          SOURCE FSTYPE OPTIONS
/etc/containers 9p     9p     rw,relatime,access=client,trans=fd,rfd=3,wfd=3
```

Stopping and restarting the machine resolves the issue.

```
C>podman machine stop && podman machine start && podman ps
Machine "podman-machine-default" stopped successfully
Starting machine "podman-machine-default"

This machine is currently configured in rootless mode. If your containers
require root permissions (e.g. ports < 1024), or if you run into compatibility
issues with non-podman clients, you can switch using the following command:

        podman machine set --rootful

API forwarding listening on: npipe:////./pipe/docker_engine
Docker API clients default to this address. You do not need to set DOCKER_HOST.

Machine "podman-machine-default" started successfully
CONTAINER ID  IMAGE       COMMAND     CREATED     STATUS      PORTS       NAMES
```


### Describe the results you received

Podman no longer works after closing the CMD.EXE process that is used to start the Podman machine.

### Describe the results you expected

Podman should keep working after closing the CMD.EXE process that is used to start the Podman machine.

The issue was also present in Podman 6.0.0.

comments.body:
Probably some sort of process keeps attached to the current console host. Time ago I had to workaround this for `qemu` by switching to `w` postfix application variants (Windows app instead of console app, which attaches to the current console host), but there is a way to start child process creating new console host and effectively detaching from the one of the current terminal - this approach is used in Lima in their Windows builds.

If this will stays unattended for 2 weeks, I can take a look when I'm back from vacation and have time to spend with my Windows machines.

Because you are using hyperV the leaked podman process should be the 9p host proxy process for the volume mount which explains why the volume becomes non functional afterwards. The process should indeed be spawned so that it is not tied to the console session like the VM or gvproxy. 

cc @l0rd @mheon

Here's the start logic: https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/blob/4d055045e5c3cb6805f52748be68e9597773d546/pkg/machine/hyperv/stubber.go#L256-L287

We need to change that to get the process into the background and detached from the current terminal session, but I'm not 100% how to do that on Windows

Hi @mheon, I’d like to work on this issue.

I looked through the latest discussion and the `hyperv/stubber.go` start path. The 9p server is currently started with `exec.Command(...).Start()` without detaching it from the parent console, which matches the reported behavior where closing CMD kills `podman.exe` while `gvproxy` remains alive.

I can take this up by fixing the Windows process creation so the 9p server survives the parent CMD/PowerShell session, and add regression coverage for the machine-start/console-close case.

Please assign it to me if it’s still available.
You can assign with `/assign` if you want - though it seems that we already have a PR
